Sourcing

Questions to ask a packaging supplier

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

Evaluate the supplier against your actual packaging project. A clear specification, relevant documents and a practical sample review are more useful than a general capability claim.

In this guideAsk about the work your project requiresCheck documents for scope and relevanceAgree on measurable sample checksKeep the order terms clearDiscuss your packaging →

Ask about the work your project requires

Share the structure, dimensions, material direction, quantity and finish before discussing capability. Ask which steps are performed by the supplier and which are handled by production partners. A rigid presentation with a fitted insert and a color-printed shipping carton may involve different equipment and quality checks.

Request examples relevant to the construction you need. A portfolio photograph can illustrate a finish but does not establish that every component will be made to the same specification. Ask what can be demonstrated through a structural sample and a decorated sample.

Check documents for scope and relevance

Confirm the legal company details and the contracting entity. When certificates or test reports are supplied, review the issuer, validity, scope and the material or product they cover. A document for one paper or factory process should not be treated as approval for a different finished pack.

Keep requests proportionate to the product and destination. If the pack has special requirements, identify them before sampling so the supplier can confirm the evidence and testing route needed for the exact order.

Agree on measurable sample checks

  • Internal fit with the actual products and accessories.
  • Closure, hinge, drawer or tuck-flap operation.
  • Paper and print reference, with approved finish positions.
  • Insert support, packing method and surface protection.
  • Inspection checkpoints and how deviations will be recorded.

Photographs help communicate a concern, but retain the approved sample as a shared reference. Write down changes made after sample review and connect them to the final artwork version.

Keep the order terms clear

Confirm pricing scope, tooling, sampling charges, quantity, schedule, payment milestones and delivery responsibilities in writing. Identify the event that starts the production schedule, such as approval of the sample and final artwork.

Before paying for production, make sure the quotation describes the pack you approved. A complete brief and orderly approval record make both the supplier review and later reorders easier to manage.
